sampling_model.design: Observational within-regime sampling from one stable equilibrium law.
sampling_model.units: \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are homogeneous iid cells or systems with fixed variable scale.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is required for SCC recovery; for predeclared distinct vertices \(u,v\in V\), a perfect intervention \(\operatorname{do}(Z_u=x)\) is used only for the union effect set for response \(v\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the statistical margin is cross-SCC covariance separation \(\delta>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Distances and effect sets optimize over every graph-specific compact parameter image; no single fitted coefficient root is treated as known.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Conjecture 5.1 states that SCC-discordant equal-outdegree noncomplete simple digraphs admit a parentally closed strict child-count gap.
The half-trek criterion is sufficient for generic identifiability and has a polynomial-time flow implementation.
Distribution equivalence for cyclic Gaussian directed graphs is characterized by support rotations under freely varying diagonal error variances.
Simple cyclic linear Gaussian graph models have the expected parameter dimension and admit score-based structure learning.
Known-block partial homoscedasticity has a necessary-and-sufficient distribution-equivalence characterization for DAGs.
Equal-variance DAG recovery follows from recursive variance ordering and sample-covariance concentration under signal and eigenvalue margins.
Goodness-of-fit inversion yields confidence sets for DAG orderings and unions of ordering-specific causal-effect intervals.
Repeated perturbation, graph screening, and unions of graph-specific intervals yield post-discovery causal-effect coverage in DAGs.
Test inversion addresses undercoverage after equal-variance causal discovery in a bivariate DAG model.

body.tldr: For labeled noncomplete simple orientations with a common Gaussian structural error variance, the proposal reduces every comparator-parent closed child-count certificate to a Hall deficiency, proves that the certificate creates an explicit precision-Jacobian rank gap, and targets the universal H-star theorem that two-sided local perfect matchings force equal SCC partitions. Conditional on H-star, the published unequal-outdegree separator yields a generic minimum-dimension covariance-model functional for feedback modules. On fixed finite compact families, cross-SCC covariance-image separation and an upper covariance-eigenvalue bound yield uniform covariance minimum-distance recovery; separate stability, edge, and scale restrictions describe the prospective SEM family but do not enter the displayed recovery bound. Split-sample procedures give honest sets of SCC partitions and union sets for equilibrium perfect-intervention effects between distinct vertices.

project_justification.gap: Static Gaussian feedback models lack a complete, polynomially certified separator for the SCC partition when two orientations have equal labeled outdegrees. The closest paper isolates this boundary as Conjecture 5.1 and proves only an acyclic-side special case.
project_justification.niche: SCCs are coarser than the full cyclic graph but retain the scientifically interpretable feedback modules. Comparator-dependent closure is strong enough to make the rank construction valid and structured enough to reduce exactly to matching.
project_justification.fill: The focal theorem is H-star, supported by the closure-to-Hall equality and the incoming-star rank minor. Conditional on proving H-star, it turns algebraic separation into a generic SCC recovery map. On fixed finite compact covariance families, the statistical bound depends on cross-SCC separation and the upper covariance-eigenvalue bound, while split-sample inversion propagates uncertainty to SCC partitions and distinct-vertex equilibrium effects.

body.related_work: Drton, Hollering, and Wu (2025) introduce the homoscedastic precision-Jacobian program, prove unequal-outdegree and parental-count separators, prove the acyclic-side graph theorem, and state the SCC boundary as Conjecture 5.1; the present kernel is informed by that boundary but uses comparator-dependent closure and does not claim that the final published equations are erroneous. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (2012) show how path feasibility, integral flow, and determinant structure can make generic SEM identification polynomially checkable; here only the matching and alternating-reachability architecture is adapted because \(\Gamma_i\)-reachability does not ensure no-sided-intersection paths. Ghassami et al. (2020) characterize cyclic Gaussian distribution equivalence when error variances vary freely, whereas the common scale defining the present varieties is load bearing. Am\'{e}ndola et al. (2020) establish expected dimension and score-based learning for simple cyclic Gaussian models. Wu and Drton (2023) characterize known-block partial homoscedasticity for DAGs; their conditional-residual argument fails inside an SCC and therefore does not occupy the present target. Chen, Drton, and Wang (2019) motivate the covariance-perturbation step but their source-peeling recursion is acyclic. Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) and Strieder et al. (2021) motivate retaining structural candidates before propagating uncertainty to effects; their formal targets are DAG orderings and bivariate DAGs. Sachs et al. (2005) provide a prospective signaling-network consumer, not evidence for the maintained within-regime Gaussian equilibrium approximation.
body.technical_internal_limitation: In the accessible arXiv-v1 proof of Theorem 4.11, a selected precision coordinate from the comparator skeleton may couple a certificate-side edge row to a parent that is a comparator neighbor but not a certificate-graph neighbor. Same-graph parental closure does not remove this coordinate. The displayed sparse comparator specialization also reverses the incoming-edge coefficient index under the paper's convention. An exact four-node recalculation gives rank five on both sides for the leaked coordinate set but ranks four and five for the corrected comparator-parent set. This diagnostic motivates Theorem 2 and is not a claim about the unaudited final journal equations or a standalone correction contribution.
body.honest_scope: H-star remains to be proved for arbitrary multiple-tail disagreements; the one-tail and maximum-outdegree-one results are sanity checks, and the replicated seeded test found no counterexample among 100,000 accepted pairs at \(p=6,7,8\) but is not proof. Generic SCC recovery is explicitly conditional on H-star and identifies only the labeled SCC partition outside a proper algebraic set, not every edge, coefficient, or causal effect. The fixed-dimensional uniform probability bound assumes a finite family of compact covariance images, iid Gaussian sampling, a positive cross-SCC covariance-image distance, and an upper covariance-eigenvalue bound; stability, edge strength, and error-scale margins do not enter that bound. Those separate SEM restrictions maintain the prospective equilibrium family and ensure the distinct-vertex effect functional is well posed. Effect sets union over all retained graphs and parameter roots and need not shrink. Reciprocal arcs, hidden confounding, heteroscedastic errors, regime pooling, time dependence, variablewise standardization, and misspecification of the equilibrium Gaussian model are outside scope.
